metaDescription: Use these field inspection and certification audit questions to verify WELL building standard cleaning protocol cost ($0.05–$0.15/sq ft). Compare quotes now.
excerpt: Paying a premium for WELL-compliant office cleaning means nothing if the night crew substitutes uncertified chemicals or bypasses HEPA filtration. Use these pre-award RFP questions, closet inspection checklists, and indoor air quality verification logs to audit your janitorial contractor.
quickAnswer: A rigorous field inspection and certification audit for WELL building standard cleaning protocol cost ensures you only pay the $0.05 to $0.15 per-square-foot compliance rate for verifiable execution. Facility managers should audit five tangible proof points every month: closed-loop chemical purchase and dilution logs (WELL Feature X09), sealed-HEPA vacuum serial inventories (Features A01/A05), enzymatic zero-VOC restroom odor controls, OSHA 1910.1200/1910.1030 staff training rosters, and live PM2.5 particulate readings during night-shift operations.

blocks.text: When a commercial office building or corporate tenant commits to the IWBI WELL Building Standard v2, the janitorial service provider typically charges a 6% to 14% operational premium over standard cleaning rates—bringing mid-size facilities (2,500 to 9,999 sq ft) to $0.10–$0.17 per square foot per visit and larger suites (10,000 to 24,999 sq ft) to $0.08–$0.13 per square foot per visit. Unfortunately, a common procurement failure across US commercial real estate is 'WELL-washing': contractors submit glossy green brochures during the RFP stage, bill higher rates ($45 to $65/hr standard or $55 to $95/hr specialty), and then send untrained night subcontractors onto the floor with ruptured paper vacuum bags and unmarked spray bottles.

Because IWBI WELL performance verification relies on both annual policy documentation (Feature X09: Cleaning Products and Protocol) and physical onsite environmental testing (Feature A01: Air Quality measuring PM2.5, PM10, and total volatile organic compounds), a single night of unauthorized bleach mopping or aerosol spraying prior to an assessor's visit can cause a failed air sample. Integrating structured vendor audit questions into your RFP and monthly Service Level Agreement (SLA) inspections protects both your certification and your operating budget.

blocks.text: 7 Pre-Award RFP Audit Questions to Eliminate Unqualified Bidders

Before awarding a 5x-week (21.65 visits/month at 0.90 frequency multiplier) or 3x-week (13.0 visits/month at 0.95 multiplier) janitorial contract, require every finalist to answer these seven operational questions in writing with attached sample logs:

items.name: Request Exact Chemical Registration Numbers and Dilution Mathematics
items.text: Ask: 'Provide the exact Green Seal GS-37, UL EcoLogo, or EPA Safer Choice registration numbers for your neutral floor cleaner, glass cleaner, restroom descaler, and breakroom degreaser, along with the diluted cost per ready-to-use gallon at your standard proportioner setting.'

items.name: Demand Serial-Numbered HEPA Vacuum and Extractor Inventories
items.text: Ask: 'List the make, model, CRI Seal of Approval tier, and filter replacement interval for every vacuum and low-moisture carpet extractor that will be stored onsite at our facility.'

items.name: Verify High-Touch Disinfection Dwell-Time Labor Allocation
items.text: Ask: 'What is the exact EPA registration number and required wet-contact dwell time of your high-touch disinfectant, and how many labor minutes per 10,000 square feet are allocated specifically to high-touch disinfection inside your 3,500 sq ft/hr ISSA production model?'

items.name: Audit Microfiber Laundering and Cross-Contamination Logistics
items.text: Ask: 'Where are soiled color-coded microfiber cloths and flat mop pads laundered, at what water temperature, and how do you guarantee fabric softeners or bleach—which destroy microfiber electrostatic charge—are never used?'

items.name: Examine Subcontractor Restrictions and Night-Shift Turnover
items.text: Ask: 'Do you W-2 employ 100% of the night crew assigned to our building, what was your account-level technician turnover rate over the past 12 months, and how is a relief cleaner briefed on our WELL Feature X09 SOP before entering the suite?'

items.name: Review OSHA HazCom, Bloodborne, and COI Documentation
items.text: Ask: 'Attach a sample Certificate of Insurance ($1M/$2M GL, statutory Workers' Comp, Janitorial Bond) and redacted OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1200 and 1910.1030 training sign-off sheets from a currently active green-certified account.'

items.name: Clarify Annual WELL Recertification Documentation Fees
items.text: Ask: 'Confirm in writing that compiling monthly chemical usage logs, consumable purchase manifests, and training rosters for our annual IWBI WELL performance verification is included in the base per-square-foot rate with zero administrative add-on fees.'

blocks.text: Using Real-Time IAQ Sensors and Enzymatic Controls to Audit Night Crews

You do not have to stand in your office at 11:00 PM every Tuesday to know whether the janitorial crew is following WELL indoor air quality rules. Continuous particulate and odor management hardware gives facility managers objective, timestamped evidence of night-shift performance:

items: Coway Airmega 400 Commercial Grade Smart HEPA Purifier: Engineered for large 1,560-square-foot open office zones and executive conference suites, this dual-suction unit pairs a Max2 Green True HEPA and activated carbon filter assembly with a real-time PM2.5 LED air quality ring. If the night crew runs a leaky non-HEPA vacuum at 9:30 PM, the onboard particulate sensor automatically ramps fan speed in Auto Mode, confirming whether airborne dust spikes occurred during cleaning.

Levoit EverestAir Commercial Large-Room HEPA Purifier: Ideal for busy 558+ square-foot reception lobbies and high-traffic wellness rooms, this commercial unit utilizes a multi-channel laser dust sensor that measures PM1.0, PM2.5, and PM10 while logging air quality trends accessible via app control—letting facility directors review overnight particulate curves from their desk the next morning.

Fresh Products Wave 3D Urinal Deodorizer Screens (10-Box): A telltale sign of poor restroom sanitation is the presence of prohibited aerosol spray cans used to cover up urine odor. These 30-day anti-splash urinal screens release beneficial bacteria and enzymatic deodorizers that eliminate odor at the source while cutting splash-back onto ceramic tile floors (1.12 flooring multiplier), keeping restroom air compliant without synthetic VOC aerosols.

blocks.title: The UV Fluorescent Marker Audit Trick
blocks.text: Before the night shift arrives on the first Wednesday of each month, apply invisible UV-reactive lotion dots to 20 high-touch targets: breakroom microwave start pads, restroom stall latches, conference room glass door pulls, and water dispenser paddles. Inspect with a blacklight flashlight at 8:00 AM. If fewer than 18 of 20 marks are completely wiped away, your vendor is collecting WELL hygiene rates for a superficial 'trash-and-dash' clean.

During your monthly 15-minute janitorial closet inspection, compare the physical fill lines on the 5-gallon concentrate pails against the square footage billed on the vendor's invoice. If a 20,000-square-foot office cleaned 5x/week (21.65 visits/month) shows zero drawdown on its neutral-pH floor concentrate pail over 45 days, the night crew is either mopping with plain tap water or bringing in unauthorized products. Tying 5% of the monthly management fee directly to passing this four-point closet and UV touchpoint audit aligns your contractor's financial incentives with your building's WELL certification.

faqs.q: How often does IWBI require cleaning logs and air quality verification under WELL v2?
faqs.a: WELL Building Standard v2 requires initial documentation and onsite performance verification at certification, followed by annual reporting of ongoing maintenance logs (such as Feature X09 chemical purchase and protocol records) and full recertification testing every three years. Conducting internal monthly vendor audits ensures your documentation is always audit-ready.

faqs.q: What should we do if our air purifier's PM2.5 sensor spikes every night during janitorial hours?
faqs.a: A consistent PM2.5 or PM10 spike between 8:00 PM and midnight almost always indicates a torn vacuum bag, a missing HEPA exhaust filter, or dry feather dusting. Inspect the night crew's vacuum canisters immediately and require the vendor to switch to sealed CRI-certified HEPA vacuums and electrostatic or damp microfiber dusting tools.

faqs.q: Can we deduct money from a janitorial invoice if the vendor fails a monthly WELL hygiene audit?
faqs.a: Yes, provided you build an objective Service Level Agreement (SLA) scorecard into your contract addendum. Standard commercial practice gives the vendor 24 hours to cure a physical cleaning defect at no charge, while repeated chemical compliance failures (such as storing bleach or unapproved aerosols onsite) trigger a 3% to 5% monthly billing credit.

faqs.q: Should our vendor supply the HEPA air purifiers or only maintain the office around them?
faqs.a: Standalone commercial HEPA air purifiers (such as units covering 558 to 1,560 sq ft in reception zones and conference rooms) are typically purchased directly by the facility or tenant as FF&E capital assets. However, you should include exterior wipe-down of purifier intakes and quarterly pre-filter vacuuming inside your janitorial contractor's regular scope of work.
